extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and researchers in partial differential equations / mathematical physics
extracted.subtask_description: Entropy-based definitions, inequalities and selection principles for parabolic and hyperbolic PDEs (heat equation, conservation laws, Boltzmann equation). Includes entropy production, H-Theorem, Harnack estimates, Clausius-type inequalities, and the entropy solution framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entropy production equation
rubrics_metrics.description: For each t ≥ 0 and each subregion V ⊂ U we have d/dt S(t,V) = F(t,V) + G(t,V) − R(t,V), where S(t,V)=∫_V log u(·,t) dx (entropy in V), F(t,V)=∫_V f(·,t)/u(·,t) dx (entropy supply), G(t,V)=∫_V γ(·,t) dx with γ = Σ_{i,j} a_{ij} u_{x_i} u_{x_j} / u^2 (internal entropy generation), and R(t,V)=−∫_{∂V} (1/u) ∂u/∂ν_A dS (entropy flux outward across ∂V).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This identity is derived by dividing the PDE by u and integrating. Use it to balance entropy change into supply, internal production, and flux across the boundary. It is the foundational balance law for subsequent monotonicity and Clausius-type estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entropy increase (Second Law for isolated domain)
rubrics_metrics.description: If f ≥ 0 in U × (0,∞) and ∂u/∂ν_A = 0 on ∂U (no-flux/insulated boundary), then S(t) = ∫_U log u(·,t) dx satisfies dS/dt ≥ 0 on [0,∞).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take V=U in the entropy production equation; the Neumann/no-flux boundary condition makes R(t,U)=0. Interpretation: entropy cannot decrease in an isolated system. The same reasoning generalizes to integrals ∫_U Φ(u(·,t)) dx for Φ with Φ' ≤ 0 and Φ'' ≥ 0 (convexity condition). If f≡0, convexity alone suffices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convex functional monotonicity criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: For any smooth Φ:(0,∞)→R with Φ' ≤ 0 and Φ'' ≥ 0, the quantity t ↦ ∫_U Φ(u(·,t)) dx is nondecreasing; if f ≡ 0 it suffices that Φ'' ≥ 0 (Φ convex).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a general convexity argument which includes the physical entropy case Φ(z)=−log z. The derivation uses multiplying the PDE by Φ'(u) and integrating; negative semidefinite gradient term appears via convexity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical interpretation mapping (modeling rubric)
rubrics_metrics.description: Interpret u as temperature, q = −A Du as heat flux, f as heat supply/unit mass; u (up to additive constants) is internal energy/unit mass and log u is entropy/unit mass; γ = Σ a_{ij} u_{x_i} u_{x_j} / u^2 is local entropy production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these identifications to translate PDE calculations into thermodynamic statements (e.g., Clausius inequality). Explicit identification conditions (e.g., cv≡1) and sign conventions are given; follow them when constructing physical analogues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monotonicity of H(t)=∫_U u log u (heat equation)
rubrics_metrics.description: If u>0 solves the heat equation ut − Δu = 0 with ∂u/∂ν = 0 on ∂U, then H(t)=∫_U u log u dx satisfies dH/dt ≤ 0 on [0,∞).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calculation uses integration by parts and the no-flux boundary condition. H(t) is used as an entropy-like quantity whose decay captures irreversibility; do not confuse with the earlier S(t)=∫ log u.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convexity in time of H(t) under convex domain
rubrics_metrics.description: If U is convex (and same hypotheses as above), then d^2H/dt^2 ≥ 0 on [0,∞) (i.e., H(t) is convex in time).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proof uses a boundary lemma (see next entry) and careful integration by parts producing nonnegative bulk terms and a boundary term controlled by convexity. The lemma condition ∂|Du|^2/∂ν ≤ 0 on ∂U is critical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boundary lemma for Neumann data (sign of normal derivative of |Du|^2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let U be smooth, bounded, convex. If u ∈ C^2(¯U) satisfies ∂u/∂ν = 0 on ∂U, then ∂|Du|^2/∂ν ≤ 0 on ∂U.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local coordinate proof: write boundary as graph of convex function γ; use tangential derivatives vanishing of ∂u/∂ν and convexity of γ to deduce sign. This lemma is used to control boundary terms in time-derivative computations for H.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differential Harnack (Li–Yau type) inequality
rubrics_metrics.description: For positive solutions u of ut − Δu = 0 in U×(0,∞) with ∂u/∂ν = 0 on ∂U and U convex, the pointwise differential inequality holds: (ut)/u + n/(2t) ≥ |Du|^2/u^2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set v = log u and w = Δv, differentiate and combine with Bochner-type inequality |Δv|^2 ≤ n|D^2v|^2 to derive a parabolic inequality for tw + n/2, then apply the maximum principle. Useful to obtain explicit pointwise control and Harnack inequalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harnack inequality (integrated corollary)
rubrics_metrics.description: For x1,x2∈¯U and 0<t1<t2, positive solution u satisfies u(x1,t1) ≤ (t2/t1)^{n/2} exp(|x2−x1|^2 / (4(t2−t1))) u(x2,t2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow from integrating the differential Harnack inequality along space-time paths and using Cauchy–Schwarz/elementary inequalities. Provide explicit Gaussian-like control in space-time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence & uniqueness of periodic cycles (prescribed boundary temperature)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given T>0 and a smooth T-periodic boundary temperature τ(t)>0, there exists a unique T-periodic solution (cycle) u of ut − Σ (a_{ij} u_{x_i})_{x_j} = 0 with u = τ on ∂U and u(·,0)=g (fixed point of time-T map).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof via solving initial-boundary value problem for each initial g and showing the time-T map Λ is a strict contraction in L^2(U) (Poincaré inequality + coercivity). Parabolic regularity upgrades the fixed point to a smooth periodic solution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clausius-type inequality for cycles
rubrics_metrics.description: For a cycle u corresponding to T-periodic τ, define Q(t)=∫_{∂U} ∂u/∂ν_A dS (total heat flux into U). Then ∫_0^T Q(t)/τ(t) dt ≤ 0, with strict inequality unless τ is constant. If τ not constant then τ_- < τ_+ (there exist temperatures at which heat is absorbed and emitted respectively).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derive by writing v=log u, using vt − div(A Dv)=γ≥0 and integrating v_t + γ ≥ (1/τ) Q(t) over one period, then integrate in time. This is the PDE analogue of the Clausius inequality from thermodynamics and relates heat flux weighted by inverse temperature to entropy production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of slowly varying cycles and near-reversibility estimate
rubrics_metrics.description: A family {τ_ε}_{0<ε≤1} is slowly varying if τ_ε is T_ε-periodic with τ_ε ≥ c>0, T_ε ≤ C/ε, and |˙τ_ε| ≤ Cε, |¨τ_ε| ≤ Cε^2. For the corresponding cycles u_ε and Q_ε(t), one has ∫_0^{T_ε} Q_ε(t)/τ_ε(t) dt = O(ε) as ε→0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretation: slowly traversed cycles approximate reversible cycles; proof uses an ansatz ũ = u_ε − τ_ε + w(x) ˙τ_ε(t) with w solving an elliptic problem, energy estimates on the remainder, and periodicity to control averaged flux. Requires control of time derivatives and period growth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boltzmann H-Theorem (entropy dissipation)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a smooth nonnegative solution f(x,v,t) of Boltzmann's equation ft + v·∇_x f = Q(f,f), the H-function H(t)=∬ f log f dv dx satisfies dH/dt ≤ 0 for t≥0; equality holds only for Maxwellians.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses the collision operator identity ∫ ψ Q(f,f) dv = (1/4)∬(f' f'_∗ − f f_∗)(ψ + ψ_∗ − ψ' − ψ'_∗) B dvdv_∗ dS and choose ψ=log f. The nonnegativity of the entropy production integral follows from monotonicity of log and B≥0. Use also ∫ Q dv = 0 for mass conservation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maxwellian characterization (equilibria for Boltzmann)
rubrics_metrics.description: A smooth nonnegative function f(v) satisfies Q(f,f) ≡ 0 iff f is a Maxwellian of the form f(v) = a e^{−b |v−c|^2} for constants a>0, b>0, c∈R^3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This identifies equilibrium distributions for kinetic models; combined with H-Theorem it suggests long-time approach to local Maxwellians (hydrodynamic closure). Use when linking kinetic H to thermodynamic entropy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thermodynamic identification: H ↔ entropy
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the Maxwellian ansatz f(x,v,t)=n(2πλ)^{−3/2} e^{−|v−ν|^2/(2λ)} and matching kinetic parameters to macroscopic temperature θ and density ρ (λ ∝ θ, nm = ρ), one obtains ρ s = −k h where h = ∫ f log f dv, hence total entropy S(t)=∫ s ρ dx = −k H(t).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides the physical interpretation that Boltzmann's H (up to constants) is the negative of thermodynamic entropy. Requires matching constants (γ=5/3 for monoatomic ideal gas) and identification κ=k/m, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integral (weak) solution definition for scalar conservation laws
rubrics_metrics.description: A function u ∈ L^1_loc(R^n×(0,∞)) is an integral solution of ut + div F(u) = 0 with initial data g if for all v∈C_c^1(R^n×[0,∞)) one has ∫_0^∞ ∫_{R^n} (u v_t + F(u)·Dv) dx dt + ∫_{R^n} g v(·,0) dx = 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the standard weak formulation (distributional solution). Examples illustrate multiple integral solutions can exist; additional selection criteria (entropy inequalities) pick the physically relevant one.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entropy/entropy-flux pair for conservation laws
rubrics_metrics.description: A pair (Φ,Ψ) is an entropy/entropy-flux pair for ut + div F(u)=0 if (i) Φ:R→R is convex and (ii) Ψ:R→R^n satisfies Ψ'(z) = b(z) Φ'(z) where b = F'. Equivalently Ψ_i(z)=∫_0^z b_i(v) Φ'(v) dv up to additive constants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entropy pairs produce conserved/monotone quantities for smooth solutions (Φ(u)_t + div Ψ(u)=0). For discontinuous solutions they motivate entropy inequalities selecting admissible shocks. Choose convex Φ to obtain dissipative inequalities from viscous approximations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entropy solution selection criterion (vanishing viscosity limit inequality)
rubrics_metrics.description: A function u∈C([0,∞); L^1(R^n)) solving ut + div F(u)=0 with initial data g is an entropy solution if for every entropy pair (Φ,Ψ) the weak inequality Φ(u)_t + div Ψ(u) ≤ 0 holds (in distributional sense) and u(·,0)=g.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Motivation: consider viscous regularizations ut + div F(u_ε) = ε Δ u_ε; convexity of Φ implies Φ(u_ε)_t + div Ψ(u_ε) ≤ ε div(Φ'(u_ε) Du_ε). Under bounds (e.g., sup_ε ε ∫ |Du_ε|^2 dx dt < ∞) one can pass to the limit and obtain the entropy inequality. This criterion selects the physically correct weak solution (rules out nonphysical shocks).

rubrics_metrics.name: Vanishing-viscosity approximate admissibility condition
rubrics_metrics.description: A limit u of viscous approximations u_ε solving ut + div F(u_ε) = ε Δ u_ε with u_ε → u boundedly a.e. and with uniform control sup_ε ε ∫ |Du_ε|^2 dx dt < ∞ satisfies the entropy inequalities and hence is an entropy solution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides a production-oriented rubric: to construct admissible solutions, regularize by viscosity, obtain uniform energy-type estimates on gradients weighted by ε, then pass to the limit. The L^2-type control (15) is singled out as a useful sufficient hypothesis.
